output: A Russian SU-27 Flanker fighter jet manoeuvred aggressively, crossing the nose of the US aircraft and exposing its armed belly, in international airspace over the Sea of Okhotsk on April 23, amid heightened tensions between the US and Russia over Ukraine.

Charles, the Prince of Wales, and his wife Camilla will visit Australia and New Zealand between November 4 and 15, meeting the new Australian PM Malcolm Turnbull, and traveling to various locations, including Wellington, Adelaide, Canberra, Sydney, Albany, and Perth.
A man, detained in Killarney, is being questioned at a Garda station in connection with an attack on a 70-year-old woman in Sneem, County Kerry, that occurred on September 20.
Former GP Hugh McGoldrick's name will be erased from the medical register because no appeal was received within the 28-day deadline.
Surrey Police is awaiting the results of a post-mortem examination after a body was discovered in a wooded area near Dorking, following the arrest of a 21-year-old male on suspicion of murder.

Josh Hanson, a 21-year-old man from north-west London, was stabbed to death at the RE bar in Eastcote on Sunday, and police are urging around 40 people who were at the scene to come forward with information.

Hovertravel, a ferry company, is considering adding a cross-Solent service between Sandown and the Isle of Wight mainland, with the goal of boosting tourism to the island, potentially operating four 25-minute crossings every Tuesday and Thursday from July to August.
A 30-year-old man was arrested and later released on bail after a victim was attacked by up to eight men in the Heights area on Sunday.

The death toll from recent floods in India has doubled over the last two days as officials found more than 100 bodies, affecting 450,000 people in the state, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi due to visit to find a permanent solution to the flooding that Assam faces every year.

Arsenal will host Leicester City on Friday 11 August, with a 19:45 BST kick-off, as the Premier League starts its new season, with Sky Sports having been awarded the rights to screen 10 Friday night matches.
Oldham Athletic Football Club has dismissed Cristian Montano, a player arrested for spot-fixing, after a thorough investigation and a decision made by the board, ahead of a big FA Cup tie.
A 20-year-old man, Rick Edwards, was given a suspended 12-month jail term and a year's supervision order for starting a fire that destroyed the 42-acre former Pontins resort at Brixham in 2014.

Wilson, a 30-year-old footballer, has been without a team since being released in May, having made 51 appearances in his second spell at Nottingham Forest, after previously playing for Celtic, Preston North End, and Notts County.

Australia's bowlers Faulkner and Amila Aponso took 3-45 and 4-18 respectively as the team secured an 82-run win over Sri Lanka in the second match of the series, leveling the five-match series at 1-1.
Sale Sharks' forward Vadim Cobilas has decided to move to France's Top 14, joining Bordeaux, after Sale boss Steve Diamond described the move as a "no-brainer" for the 32-year-old.
India, chasing 349, collapsed from 277-1 to 323 all out, with Australia's Kane Richardson taking 5-68, after a 212-run partnership between Virat Kohli and Shikhar Dhawan earlier in the match.
The Hammersmith and City Line and parts of the Circle Line have been suspended due to concerns over debris from a 24-storey block fire in London, which has claimed at least 58 presumed lives.
Jamie Hamill, a 27-year-old, has signed a three-year contract with Kilmarnock, where he will make his 150th appearance for the club, marking his second time playing for the team.
Ipswich fan Ross Morgan accidentally punched a hole in his ceiling during a match, but was surprised and grateful when goal-scorer Paul Anderson offered to pay for the repairs.
In Wales, a new law requires retailers to keep cigarettes out of public view, with shop managers and assistants facing fines of up to £5,000 and six months in prison if they fail to comply.
A 20-year-old Lucas has had two previous spells with Bristol Rovers and scored three goals in 10 appearances for the National League side this season.

Work is being carried out at Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire, including making the station watertight and removing and rebuilding the chimney stack on the signal box, with work on the platform canopy to be carried out at night.

Lawrence Phillips, a former NFL player and convicted felon, was found dead in a cell, with officials believing he took his own life, despite being accused of killing his former cellmate and having a history of violent behavior.

The Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT) plan proposes extending bus lane operating hours from 07:00 to 19:00, and is due to come into operation in September 2018, with plans for two rounds of consultation to consider ideas such as loading and unloading windows.

Lionel Messi scored the winning goal in Barcelona's match against Atletico, scoring his 287th La Liga goal for the club after being set up by Luis Suarez, on the day that Cristiano Ronaldo became Real Madrid's record league scorer.

Those arrested in a match-fixing inquiry led by prosecutors in Catanzaro are suspected of 'conspiracy to commit sporting fraud' and include players and directors from around 30 clubs, some of whom had links to mafia organisations.

Approximately 1,600 Dolomedes plantarius spiderlings, bred as hybrids between species from Sussex and Suffolk, have been released into suitable dykes at Castle Marshes to give the new population the best potential to adapt to its surroundings and to cope with the impacts of climate change.
In 1947, the Partition of India led to the independence of two new countries, resulting in millions of people becoming refugees as they were forced to leave their homes due to the separation.

Iva Barr, a 30-year marathon veteran who participated in the first London Marathon in 1981, completed about 14 miles of the course before taking an Underground train and walking the final part to the finish line, calling the experience "wonderful".
In China's top cities, the extremely high demand for property has led to some couples undergoing fake divorces to buy additional homes, despite the central bank's efforts to control rising prices.

A 46-year-old landlord, Mr Jones, died at a pub in Holyhead, and a 24-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder after a stand-off with police, with police appealing for witnesses from a nearby bus.
The BBC News Entertainment team provides contact information, inviting readers to follow them on social media and email story suggestions.

A fatal car crash occurred on the A713 near Carsphairn, Scotland, when a red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided, resulting in the deaths of both drivers, a 50-year-old man and a 46-year-old man from Ayrshire.
Australian rower Sarah Tait, who was diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013, was remembered as an inspirational and strong role model by her peers, including Olympic champion Helen Glover.

A suicide bomber hit a bus in western Kabul, largely destroying it, and another bus was hit elsewhere in the city, injuring two soldiers and two civilians in each attack, as the Taliban claimed responsibility for the two incidents, which occurred a day after at least 15 people were killed in Kabul and Paktia provinces, following the signing of a US-Afghan agreement allowing US troops to stay in the country beyond 2014.

Daimler, the parent company of Mercedes-Benz, reported a 6% increase in sales of its cars and commercial vehicles in the second quarter, with the company predicting that its full-year sales will be "significantly more than 100bn euros" despite a slowdown in sales in China.

A 10-year-old son of Danish Crown Prince Frederik was saved by a lifeguard, Nick Malcolm, at Mermaid Beach after being caught in a rip current, with officials initially downplaying the incident but later acknowledging the potential severity of the situation.
A fire at a property in Elgin Road, Scotland, resulted in the discovery of an elderly man's body, with police indicating that there are no initial signs of suspicious circumstances.

Veterans with amputation-related medical issues can now access specialized treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) in Surrey, following a new program aimed at providing the best possible care for those who have made significant sacrifices for Britain's safety.

Over 125 drivers per day have been caught by enforcement cameras on a two-mile stretch in Port Talbot, Wales, following a clear indication that the number of drivers exceeding the limit has decreased from around 700 drivers a day caught in a previous trial period.

A Manchester-born teacher, who had previously lived in the Seville area, was arrested in Valladolid as part of an Interpol investigation, suspected of secretly taking photographs of his students and possessing a large number of sexually explicit files involving minors, and police are still trying to establish the identity of the victims shown in the images found on his electronic devices.

A sturgeon named Steve, who escaped from a water centre in Romsey, Hampshire due to flooding, has been found in a car wash near the centre, where centre manager Mark Bradbury was "hugely relieved" to report that Steve was "only a little worse for wear for his travels".
Comedian Chris Rock has filed for divorce from his wife Malaak Compton-Rock, who he has been married to for 19 years, and is requesting privacy as he and his wife work through the process.
A multi-vehicle collision on the motorway at Tamnamore, near junctions 13 and 14, has caused the road to be closed in both directions, resulting in significant traffic congestion.

The French government has nominated senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini as ambassador to the Vatican, but the Vatican has yet to respond, sparking speculation that the long silence may indicate a rejection of the nomination.

The Nasdaq index experienced its largest one-day decline since April 10 last year, falling 2.4% or 118 points to 4,876, while the Dow Jones and S&P 500 also saw losses, due in part to declines in semiconductor and biotech stocks.

Marketa Vondrousova edged Estonia's 99th-ranked Kontaveit 6-4 7-6 (8-6), while Borna Coric saved five match points to defeat Germany's Philipp Kohlschreiber at the Grand Prix Hassan II in Marrakech, clinching his first ATP title.
Stoke City has signed 28-year-old striker Eric Choupo-Moting, a former Germany youth international who has played in the Bundesliga and Champions League, as their fourth signing of the summer.

A 56-year-old man, Seamus McCollum, who had cerebral palsy and lived in a private nursing home in Randalstown, was reclassified as a murder investigation after an autopsy in April revealed his death was suspicious, following his death in September.

Heavy rains triggered by a depression in the Bay of Bengal have brought Chennai to a standstill, affecting over 80,000 people and prompting the Tamil Nadu government to announce a 5bn-rupee relief fund.

A bus caught fire on the A760 Kilbirnie Road near Largs, Scotland, on Saturday, but thanks to the driver's quick actions, all passengers, including a partially-sighted woman, were safely evacuated with no injuries reported.

Jake Ball, a 25-year-old English cricketer, has made a strong start to the 2016 County Championship season, taking six wickets in each of Notts' first two games and impressing his team's coaches with his form and potential to lead the bowling attack.

A memorial stone, made from Jersey granite, has been unveiled in the French village of Guillemont to commemorate the 120 "Jersey Pals" who died during the Battle of the Somme, with a portion of the stone to be returned to Jersey to become part of a monument in Royal Square.
John Boyega, who played stormtrooper Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens, spoke to Theatre Peckham about his experience and expressed his honour to be in a position to give back.
Aphibarnrat moved a shot ahead of Fitzpatrick after a 40-foot breaking birdie putt at 14, with Luke Donald four shots adrift and Lee Westwood two shots further back.

Middlesex ended day one of their County Championship match against Hampshire in a strong position, with Voges unbeaten on 128 and the hosts having reached 342-3, thanks in part to a 279-run partnership between Voges and Malan.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is in critical condition in hospital following an incident in Penilee Road, while a 54-year-old man wanted for questioning has been located in the Dumfries and Galloway area.

A three-bedroom house at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, where a member of The Beatles lived from birth until they were five years old, has been sold to an anonymous telephone bidder at a Countrywide Property Auction, with a guide price of between £150,000 and £250,000.

Aaron Joseph, 29, denied being the owner of a dog that caused injury while the dog was dangerously out of control in a public place, and a trial date has been set for 5 February, in connection with a fatal incident last August, in which the dog's owner, David Ellam, was killed.
A 22-year-old man from Shrewsbury, Thomas Bebbington, was found deceased on private land near Leighton, about 10 miles away from the town center, after being reported missing on November 10.
Five-week-old baby otters are doing well, still need six feeds each day, and are not expected to be able to survive on their own until the summer.
Police in Newtownards are seeking witnesses to a bonfire disturbance and potential activity around the home of 33-year-old Joanne Thompson, who was found deceased on Wednesday.

Approximately 2,270 black-tailed godwits were spotted on the Scottish island of Tiree this spring, more than double the previous record, with many of the birds believed to be stopping over to refuel before migrating to Iceland.
Ian Durrant will not be returning to Rangers after spending last season in charge of the Under-20 development squad, as manager Mark Warburton is altering the coaching personnel.
A rare albino deer has been born, with biologists estimating that such occurrences happen only once every 100,000 births, drawing attention from visitors.

Asad Khan, a student at Beckfoot Upper Heaton School in Bradford, died after being found by his mother, with his family claiming he had been bullied, and the coroner is considering calling a witness who allegedly spoke to Asad about his difficulties.

A painting, depicting the 1654 ceremony, had hung at Rokeby Park since at least 1880, with its ownership history and the identity of its artist remaining a mystery, and its value yet to be determined.

Macclesfield Town won 3-0 against Wrexham, with Danny Rowe scoring after the break, followed by Mitch Hancox shortly after, and Danny Whittaker's shot putting the result beyond doubt before the end of the match.

French oil and gas company Total has partnered with the Confederation of African Football (Caf) as the new headline sponsor, starting with the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations finals in Gabon and covering its 10 competitions.

Spain's national team manager, Julen Lopetegui, has recalled Diego Costa and Juan Mata, and added players including David de Gea, David Silva, and Cesar Azpilicueta to the squad for a friendly against Belgium and their first World Cup qualifier against Liechtenstein.

A large wildfire, believed to have been started deliberately, has spread across a 5-kilometre area in a border region, prompting an appeal from authorities for the public to report any further instances of reckless behavior.

Boyd Rankin, who previously played for England, is returning to Ireland, becoming eligible to play again under ICC regulations on 18 January 2016, and will now be available for the InterContinental Cup match with Papua New Guinea and the ICC World Twenty20 in March.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, created with the Patient Client Council, aims to provide an independent voice and improve treatment and care for individuals and families affected by rare diseases in Northern Ireland.

Gloucester Cathedral, established by Henry VIII in 1539, is planning to include girl choristers in its choir, currently made up of 20 boys and 12 adults, as part of an exciting new chapter in its history.

Pedro, a 29-year-old Chelsea winger, was taken to hospital following a game in Beijing and stayed overnight due to a head injury, but posted a message saying "everything is OK" before travelling back to London, and is expected to return to training with a protective mask.

Nottinghamshire has appointed former England cricketer James Taylor as a batting coach, and former Northants captain David Sales will also work with the county's batsmen, bringing their expertise to improve the team's performance.

A man has been charged with two counts of criminal damage, disorderly behaviour, and assault on police, following an incident on Whiterock Road in Belfast, and is due to appear in court on December 5.
A volunteer crew from the Larne RNLI launched two lifeboats to assist a yacht whose engine failed a mile north east of Muck Island, towing it to Carrick Marina.
Ipswich Town was ahead after David McGoldrick's volley, but MK Dons equalized through Revell's penalty, before Ipswich regained the lead with Brett Pitman's glancing header.

A man from Darlington has been issued a summons to appear in court on charges of dangerous driving, causing serious injury by dangerous driving, and three counts of criminal damage, following the fall of a bridge onto the London-bound carriageway, between junctions 4 and 3 of the M25 motorway, which injured a motorcyclist who suffered broken ribs.

A group of approximately 200 people, organized by several Germans, staged a flashmob in Platja d'Aro, Spain, pretending to be paparazzi chasing a celebrity, which led to panic and chaos among bystanders, resulting in injuries and a police response.

Sindyann Regis, 25, of High Street, Wednesfield, and Chevaze Mcgregor, 27, of New Road in Rainford, Essex, appeared at Wolverhampton Crown Court charged with the murder of two-and-a-half-year-old Jeremiah Regis, who was found injured and later died from abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma.

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common in Devon has engulfed a significant area, with firefighters battling the flames in multiple fronts, and multiple people have been treated for smoke inhalation and burns.

The British Speedway Promoters' Association has announced that an agreement has been reached, with a 15-year lease also signed for the team's venue, and chairman Keith Chapman hopes for a "new start" for the club.
A 50-year-old woman, Elizabeth Bowe, was found badly injured in her home in St Andrews and later died, and her brother, Charles Gordon, has been charged with her murder and remanded in custody.

Ross County manager Jim McIntyre has signed 29-year-old midfielder Jim O'Brien on a two-year contract, having previously signed him on loan last season, during which he made 18 appearances and scored twice.

Northants' seam attack took advantage of Durham's fragile batting line-up, restricting the visitors to 59-3, 107 runs behind, before Max Holden and Chesney Hughes helped limit the damage in the first day of the match.
New Zealand's Lydia Ko is one shot behind joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim after two rounds at the women's major in Seattle, with only five players under par.
Gordon Watson, a 56-year-old former coach, has rejoined the Scotland national team as an assistant to manager Gordon Strachan, marking his second stint with the team.

The Belfast Giants took an early lead through Colin Shields before Scott Aarssen levelled late in the first period, but the Giants then extended their lead to 4-1 through second-period goals from Ryan Martinelli and Mark Garside.
Defending champion Jordan Spieth had a quadruple-bogey seven on the par-three 12th as Danny Willett became the first Englishman since Faldo's 1996 win to claim the Masters title.

The BBC is accepting picture submissions for England's Big Picture through various social media platforms and email, but requires contributors to grant a royalty-free license to publish their work and adhere to certain guidelines and terms.

An optometrist, Honey Rose, is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter after a routine eye test allegedly failed to detect a patient's swollen optic discs, leading to the patient's death five months later.
Food price inflation rose to 4.9% in June, above expectations, which reduces the prospect of interest rate cuts and may lead to a neutral monetary policy.
Ivory Coast international Cheick Tiote, a former Newcastle player, died after collapsing during training with Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on June 5, aged 30.
Slovak Sagan won the stage of the Tour de France, with Thibaut Pinot moving to second overall behind leader Nairo Quintana.

Cuadrilla's plans for fracking at its Preston New Road site in Lancashire have been approved, with the company promising to put Lancashire first for creating jobs, new skills, investment, and community initiatives.

Two 17-year-old males and a 19-year-old male from north-west London, who were reported missing amid fears they were planning to travel to Syria, were arrested and later released without charge after being stopped by Turkish officials at Istanbul's Sabiha Gokcen airport.

A respiratory consultant at the Royal Berkshire Hospital, Dr Christopher Davies, commented on a £22.95 quote for a blackout blind, saying it was excessive due to its likely high quality, as he noted the price suggested the blind "must have been gold plated".

The Swansea City development squad celebrated 31 wins across all competitions in 2016-17, after their senior team survived in the Premier League due to Crystal Palace beating Hull, and the "young Swans" celebrated the cup final win, which was one of the 31 wins.

Denbighshire councillors are considering creating a secondary dune system at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn to strengthen defences and reduce the risk of flooding, following severe storms in December 2013.

South Shields will host the tie on 19 August, with commentary by Conor McNamara and Danny Webber, and a game from every stage of the 2017-18 tournament will be streamed live across BBC Sport's digital platforms.

Police in Scotland are investigating a targeted attack on a property in which a 38-year-old man suffered serious facial injuries and a 49-year-old man was not injured, with officers appealing for witnesses and information about suspicious vehicles.
Pamela McLaggan pleaded guilty to manslaughter after being accused of killing Jonathan Baines, whose body was found at a house in Gainsborough on August 1.

A 15-year-old boy was assaulted at Patterton station on October 3, suffering facial injuries, after an altercation between his group and a group of older people on a train from Glasgow Central to Neilston.

A 17-year-old boy from Dewsbury was questioned in April under section 5 of the Terrorism Act, and Hassan Munshi and another 17-year-old boy, Talha Asmal, are feared to have travelled to Syria to join the Islamic State in March.

GB has announced a 22-man squad for matches against hosts Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia between 11-14 February, featuring three Giants' forwards and the return of netminder Stephen Murphy from injury.
Matthew Perry may tape something for a tribute special to James Burrows, the creator of the sitcom "Friends", which is set to air on NBC on 21 February.

Jones, a 31-year-old player who started his career at Manchester United, made 41 league appearances for Burnley last season, as they won the Championship title, and he started their Premier League defeat by Swansea on Saturday.
A Melbourne lawyer, Joe Acquaro, was found shot dead outside a cafe he owned, with investigators suggesting that underworld bosses may have put a price on his head.

Air France flight AF374, carrying 294 passengers from Paris to Vancouver, was diverted to Prestwick after the cabin crew detected a slight smell of burning on board, and passengers were then flown back to Charles de Gaulle Airport on a second aircraft.

The remains of Hurricane Gonzalo are expected to bring strong winds and heavy rain to the UK, particularly to coastal areas and north-western Wales, with the worst weather conditions likely on Tuesday.
Some people are concerned that overcrowding in hospitals is causing long wait times for patients, including children who require medical attention after injuries.

A 64-year-old man, Kenneth David Dickie, was found with a serious head injury on Sunday 8 May at the Rockley Park site in Poole and died from his injuries on Saturday, and a 34-year-old man has been charged with causing grievous bodily harm, while a 57-year-old woman has been arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent and perverting the course of justice.

Former Manchester United forward Matteo Macheda will stay at the City Ground until the end of the season, and there would be a 24-hour recall clause in any deal that would allow Cardiff to rejoin him.

The body of Christopher Huxtable, a 34-year-old man from Swansea who had been missing since a building collapse in February, was finally found and recovered, bringing closure to his family, while two other men, Ken Cresswell and John Shaw, remain missing.
Bristol City head coach Lee Johnson emphasizes the importance of a win against QPR, which could significantly improve their position in the league and draw other teams into the competition.

ESA astronaut Luca described walking in space as "absolutely fantastic" and was "giddy with excitement", having taken part in two spacewalks, orbited the Earth 2,656 times, and traveled more than 110 million kilometers during his mission.

Joe Arundel, a player who made his debut for the Tigers at 16 and went on to make 44 appearances for them, has joined Hull FC, and the club's director of rugby, Shaun McRae, sees him as a key part of their long-term plans.

Ulster Bank, a subsidiary of the RBS group, is working to resolve an issue affecting around 600,000 payments, with customers advised to visit a branch or contact call centers, and the bank promising no customers will be left out of pocket.
Tanzania led Kenya in the 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, with Omari Mwanahamisi scoring two goals, as Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1 in a play-off for third place.

McDonald's Japan is rationing French fries due to a shortage caused by industrial action in America, which has reduced the availability of potatoes, and is importing extra potatoes to try to meet demand.

The total purse for the Classic on June 3 will be £1.625m due to the addition of Permian and Khalidi, and trainer John Jenkins is defending the decision to run 1,000-1 outsider Diore Lia, with John Gosden's Cracksman currently favourite.
Griezmann will miss France's friendly against Ivory Coast due to a haematoma on his left foot, with an injury to the bone ruled out after an X-ray.
The Manly Sea Eagles' coach Laurent Frayssinous has welcomed veteran front-rower Willie Mason, who played 290 NRL games and 24 tests for the Kangaroos, to the club.
A new survey by the Marine Conservation Society shows an overall 11% increase in dog mess on UK beaches, with a 71% increase in Scotland, but also notes a decrease in overall litter levels this year.

The UK Supreme Court ruled that the government's introduction of court fees in 2013 was unlawful and unconstitutional, as it indirectly discriminated against women by making it more expensive for them to pursue discrimination cases.

Wycombe won the match against Dagenham & Redbridge, with Paris Cowan-Hall scoring the winning goal after Dagenham had drawn level, moving Wycombe up to sixth spot and leaving Dagenham in the relegation places.

Bee-eaters, a native species to southern Europe, have successfully bred at Low Gelt Quarry in the UK, with chicks expected to fledge in the next few weeks, marking the second time they have done so in the UK.

A boy jumped into the River Wey in Guildford to try to save his father after his father's boat capsized, but was advised by members of the public to return to safety, with a search operation now underway to locate the missing kayaker.
A girl visiting Rabat Zoo was fatally struck by a stone that got past the elephant's fence and a ditch, possibly as a result of the elephant's frustration.

Ms Glass, MP for North West Durham, has been appointed as a shadow minister for Europe and a shadow junior education minister, succeeding her predecessor, who resigned citing that Jeremy Corbyn's position as party leader had become "untenable" and that she did not have confidence that he could provide an effective opposition.
Chelsea manager Conte believes six teams, including Tottenham, Manchester United, Manchester City, Arsenal, Liverpool, and Chelsea, can "fight to win the title" in the Premier League.

A dispersal order has been issued in Llangefni, allowing police and community support officers to force troublemakers to leave the area, protecting young people from the excesses of alcohol and its potential consequences, and taking measures to address repeat issues of anti-social behaviour, including taking individuals under 16 home or to a place of safety, banning individuals from the area for up to 24 hours, and allowing for arrest if they return.
Boro's manager Garry Monk has confirmed that Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker is a target, one of many the club has had throughout the summer months.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, established in 2008 to reward authors and artists of humorous children's books, is set to be relaunched in 2016 as part of Roald Dahl's centenary celebrations with the goal of ensuring its continued success.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr., a 74-year-old white supremacist, was sentenced to death by lethal injection for the 2014 murders of three people, including a 14-year-old boy and a 69-year-old man, outside Jewish facilities in Kansas.

A city council plans to introduce a self-service bike scheme, which will be far larger than the initial pilot scheme, with 500 self-service bikes to be located across the city, and aims to secure a provider to operate the scheme, which will be financed through sponsorship income.

West Ham's Diafra Sakho has returned to light training after back surgery and is essentially starting his own pre-season training schedule, requiring several weeks to build up his strength and fitness before being considered for selection.

In Northern Ireland, property prices rose by 5.4% annually in the third quarter, with the average standardised price across all property types reaching just over £124,000, and prices were almost flat compared to the second quarter of the year, rising by 0.8%.
A lorry delivering a huge wind turbine part ended up in a ditch on Bargrennan Bridge near Newton Stewart, highlighting the perils of delivering such large items on country roads.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board has suggested downgrading services at one of its district hospitals, Glan Clwyd Hospital, due to a staffing shortage, but is facing opposition from residents who are concerned about the impact on local maternity care.
Mignon du Preez scored 116 off 99 balls to help South Africa post a commanding total of 272-6 against Ireland in the second ODI, before the Proteas bowlers restricted Ireland to 204.

Peake, a 30-year-old athlete who currently holds the Welsh record, aims to break her own record at the Cardiff International Sports Stadium and reach the Rio Olympics by meeting the qualification standard of 4.50m set by British Athletics.
A fire that burned for over 10 hours at a building site in Llanwern was extinguished, and police are investigating the blaze, which is believed to have been deliberately set.
A charity event was held in Edinburgh to raise money for the Nepal earthquake relief effort, organized by Mercy Corps in collaboration with the Nepal Scotland Association and the city council.

Hibernian head coach Neil Lennon has been suspended by Uefa for "acts of violence against the referee" following his remonstrating with officials during a match against Brondby, and the club has announced plans to appeal the decision.

A fire broke out at the ICL UK Boulby mine, one of Europe's deepest mines, on April 13, resulting in seven workers being hospitalized for smoke inhalation and a notice being served by the Health and Safety Executive for the company to improve procedures.
A 23-year-old British tourist and a French tourist were caught posing naked at Machu Picchu by surveillance workers, and the British Foreign Office is in contact with local authorities in Peru.
Croatian midfielder Ivan Rakitic is set to sign a new deal with Barcelona on Friday, which includes a £109m (125m euros) buyout clause.

A couple from Halstead suffered "life-changing" injuries during "two hours of torture" on 26 April, and police have released a computer-generated image of one of the suspects, a black man, around 5ft 10in tall, created with the help of one of the victims.

The Wickerman Festival, taking place on July 25 and 26 at East Kirkcarswell Farm near Dundrennan, has announced its lineup, featuring Dizzee Rascal as the opening night headliner, alongside other acts such as Martha Reeves and The Vandellas and Big Country.
Foden, a 26-year-old rugby player, expressed hope that his performance and that of his Saints teammates will lead to a strong England rugby team in the Six Nations tournament.
A 22-year-old motorcyclist died after a collision involving a KTM motorcycle and a Vauxhall Zafira car in Dagenham, while a 10-year-old boy in the car remains in serious condition.

Pfizer has agreed a deal with California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals to acquire the company, with its flagship eczema cream, crisaborole, expected to generate up to $2 billion in annual sales if approved by US regulators.
Police in Dagenham arrested two teenage boys, aged 17 and 15, after a street fight on Saturday, recovering three large knives, scissors, and cannabis from the scene.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff has been arrested on suspicion of sexual assault after a 19-year-old woman was allegedly attacked near Cardiff Civic Centre.

A by-election will be held in the Ettrick, Roxburgh and Berwickshire constituency after Conservative MSP John Lamont resigned to contest the Westminster seat, where he will seek to unseat the SNP's Calum Kerr.
Canada has opened its market to beef imports from the EU's biggest producers, France and Germany, as part of a growing trend to recognise the EU's robust measures to eradicate BSE.

European finance ministers have endorsed a move to be completed by the end of the summer, which includes creating a single EU list of "non-cooperative jurisdictions" and a crackdown on banks and tax advisers who help clients hide money offshore, as part of efforts to address the issue of tax havens revealed by the Panama Papers leak.

Archaeologists working near Inverness, Scotland, have uncovered Bronze Age burnt mounds, pottery fragments, and kilns, which are associated with ancient practices that may have included heating stones in water-filled pits.
Main scored after the hour mark, securing victory for the Latics as they have a sizeable cushion above the relegation places.
Pierce Lally, a renowned Irish actor, passed away peacefully in hospital after a short illness, leaving behind a legacy of notable roles in Irish and international productions.

Derby City Council's initial plan to close Moorways Pool due to budget constraints has been averted after campaigners gathered over 4,000 signatures on a petition, with the council committing to keep it open for a year after finding savings through cuts in back-office areas and management job restructuring.

Nottingham-born actress Vicky McClure was ordered off a tram in 2015 after being challenged for fare evasion, despite having been offered a free ride following a ceremony to unveil the tram, with the travel officer unaware of her special status.

An inquest into the 2014 death of 14-year-old Alice Gross will examine whether government and police failures contributed to her death, and why a convicted Latvian murderer, Arnis Zalkalns, was not monitored or known about, raising concerns about the robustness of systems for monitoring foreign offenders and cross-border information sharing.

Research by The Local Data Company and the University of Stirling found that Scotland's average retail vacancy rate dropped from 14.5% to 13.7%, with Anstruther, Clydebank, Dumfries, Inverkeithing, Lochgelly, Peterhead, and Pitlochry being among the most improved towns, while East Kilbride has the highest rate of all Scottish towns at 33% and towns such as Banff, Dumbarton, Cumbernauld, and Ardrossan have maintained a vacancy rate above 22% over the last three years.

Rory McWhirter, who was sentenced after collecting identity details from people and using them to register fake births, claim £14,222 in tax credits, £19,658 in child benefits, and a £500 Sure Start maternity grant, was described by the Sheriff as having committed a "fairly sophisticated" fraudulent scheme.

Clashes between Saudi security forces and Shia residents in the Eastern Province have escalated, resulting in at least seven deaths and widespread damage, amid allegations of forced displacement and human rights abuses in the city of Awamiya.

Young people in Northern Ireland, such as Donna Rennie, Marc Young, William Glass, Thomas McKeown, and Dylan Bell, are expressing frustration about their struggles to find employment and feel that politicians should be doing more to address their concerns and create opportunities for them.

The chief executive of Barnet Council, Andrew Travers, left the authority by "mutual agreement" after an election day error attributed to electoral registration lists, which initially affected many voters who were turned away from polling stations, with some stations reporting that only a small proportion of early voters were able to cast their ballots.

Cardiff City manager Neil Warnock has given midfielder Peter Whittingham time to consider a new contract offer, saying the decision ultimately lies with the player and the offer will remain on the table.

A BBC and BuzzFeed News investigation has revealed evidence of suspected match-fixing in elite tennis, prompting doubles representative Jamie Fleming to express concerns and call for increased funding for the Tennis Integrity Unit to police the sport.

A 60-year-old man, who is believed to be from the local area and a customer at the bank branch, surrendered to police after producing a firearm in a bank branch in Northfield, Birmingham, and was taken to hospital for an assessment before being questioned later.

Mohammed Ali, a 31-year-old computer software programmer from Liverpool, has denied attempting to possess a chemical weapon, specifically 500mg of the deadly toxin ricin, which he allegedly ordered from a black market dealer who was actually an FBI agent.

The chief executive of Rodney Parade Limited, which owns the stadium used by Newport County, responded to the team's manager questioning the value of their leasing deal, stating that the cost of maintaining the pitch outweighs the revenue they receive from the football club.

A survey by Aviva UK Health found that 69% of those asked said they had worked when unwell, with many fearing a heavy workload upon their return, highlighting the issue of "presenteeism" that can negatively impact business performance.

The Bank of England trimmed its 2017 growth forecast due to household spending slowing more quickly than expected, while Hikma dropped 8.2% due to US regulators delaying approval for a new drug and Centrica fell 5.4% after JP Morgan cut its rating.

Seleznev, the son of a Russian MP, has been found guilty of hacking into US pizza chains in Washington state, stealing and selling almost 3 million credit card numbers, and will face a mandatory jail term of four years when sentenced on December 2.

US President Donald Trump denied making and having any recordings of conversations with former FBI Director James Comey, in a tweet that followed his earlier statement from May, where he hinted that there may be recordings of their meetings.

Liberty, a global steel and commodities business led by Sanjeev Gupta, is preparing to submit a bid for Tata's remaining UK steel assets, including the Port Talbot factory, with the government offering to take a 25% stake and provide hundreds of millions of pounds in finance.

The 19 councils in the East Midlands region have described a light rail tram scheme as one of their "priority projects" in devolution negotiations, which would run to East Midlands Airport and the proposed HS2 station at Toton, with estimated costs mentioned for separate lines (£180m for a line from Nottingham to Ripley and £200m for a link from Toton to Derby).

Ronnie O'Sullivan, the five-time world champion, won the Masters tournament by beating Barry Hawkins 10-1, attributing his victory to his ability to modify his game and add power to it, and stating that it has given him massive confidence despite struggling with injury.

Severe storms in Poland have killed six people, damaged thousands of homes, and brought down over eight million cubic meters of lumber across 45,000 hectares of forest, with Poland's chief forester estimating it will take up to two years to clear the fallen trees.

Latin singer Enrique Iglesias suffered a fracture and required reconstructive surgery after attempting to grab a drone camera at a concert in Tijuana, Mexico, and will be recovering during the next few weeks, with a full recovery anticipated.
The Leeds Rhinos dominated Warrington Wolves in a Super League match, winning with a score of 12-0 at half-time, with Matt Parcell scoring a hat-trick and Joel Moon scoring his 15th try in 16 games.

William "Plum" Smith, who played a central role in the 1994 ceasefire of loyalist paramilitary groups, has passed away, with his commitment to peace and politics in Northern Ireland widely praised by those who knew him.

Olive Cooke, a 92-year-old British woman, has been a dedicated member of the Royal British Legion since age 16, motivated by the memory of her first husband who was killed in action in 1943, and has been selling poppies from the entrance to Bristol Cathedral for the past 12 years, providing more than 75 years of support to the Royal British Legion and their annual Poppy Appeal.

Shimon Peres, a Nobel Peace Prize-winning Israeli politician who served as prime minister and president, has died, leaving behind a legacy marked by his long-standing commitment to promoting peace and compromise between Israel and the Palestinians.

A survey of Queen's University staff in Northern Ireland found mixed results, with 70% of staff participating, but only 29% agreeing that senior leaders provided effective leadership, while staff were more positive about aspects such as their work being interesting and the university's standing in Northern Ireland.

The US Navy's X-47B jet, designed by Northrop Grumman, successfully completed its maiden flight, reaching 5,000 feet and lasting 29 minutes, marking a significant step towards developing a new generation of unmanned drones with advanced capabilities.

Airbus has reduced deliveries of the A380 from 15 this year to 12 in 2018 and eight in 2019, citing low prospects for short-term sales, and posted second-quarter operating profits which fell 27% to 859m euros, as rival Boeing's shares had already hit a record high on Wednesday.

Scientists have found that 40% of coral has died at the Dongsha Atoll in the South China Sea, where a high-pressure system led to devastating effects, highlighting the potential inadequacy of a 2-degree cap on ocean warming to save coral reefs due to the unique characteristics of shallow water ecosystems.

Scientists from the University of Queensland and Monash University have recreated a protein, Hi1a, from the venom gland of Australian funnel web spiders, which has shown promise as a potential treatment for stroke by blocking acid-sensing ion channels in the brain, although it is still at the early stages of research and its effectiveness in humans remains to be determined.
Oldham Athletic took an early lead through Peter Clarke's downward header in the fifth minute, but Bradford City dominated the rest of the game and equalised with a penalty in the 57th minute.

Researchers have found that the drug aducanumab, which targets the build-up of amyloid in the brain, is safe and hints at halting memory decline, but its effectiveness requires further testing, including larger studies to evaluate its effects and confirm its potential to slow cognitive decline.
Oldham Roughyeds led 24-6 at the break and ultimately secured a victory over Hull KR in the Challenge Cup, with Gary Middlehurst and Lepori's second try proving decisive for the part-time side.

BBC director general Tony Hall outlined plans for the corporation to become an "open BBC for the internet age," including initiatives such as an Ideas Service and partnerships with local newspapers, but also warned that funding cuts would likely lead to the loss or reduction of some services.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission has expressed concern over a rise in hate attacks since the UK's EU referendum, calling for politicians to engage in "accurate information and respectful debate" to address the issue and prevent further polarization.

Diane Evans, who is currently suspended from UKIP, has given up hope of becoming the party's leader, citing the actions of a "handful of people at the top" who have prevented her from running, and has endorsed councillor Lisa Duffy as her preferred candidate to succeed Nigel Farage.

A new grading system for GCSE exams in England will use numbers from 1 to 9 instead of letters, and coursework will be scrapped for most subjects, with the changes applying to pupils who turn 13 in the 2014-2015 academic year, starting with new courses in English language, English literature, and maths from autumn 2015, and with the first exams for those taken in 2017 and 2018 being graded with numbers.

Gen Petraeus expressed his willingness to serve under President Trump, saying that if asked, one must put aside reservations and serve the country, and also compared Trump's potential outreach to Russia to President Nixon's overtures to China, while warning that any such move should be attempted "with your eyes wide open".

US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton has met with Egyptian President Mohammed Mursi, urging compromise and real politics to prevent confrontation between Mursi's supporters and the country's military rulers.

Derek Bruder, a witness to the Hillsborough disaster, has testified that he was pressured by a police inspector, Matthew Sawers, to change his statement about the events surrounding the death of 15-year-old Kevin Williams, claiming that the inspector's visit left him "confused" and led him to concede that Kevin may not have been alive when he tried to revive him.

The British indie-pop duo Oh Wonder, composed of Josephine and her musical partner Anthony West, wrote their new album "Ultralife" after experiencing a whirlwind two years of online success, resulting in a record deal and a world tour, and drawing inspiration from their experiences and themes of human connection in their music.
Chelsea drew 1-1 with Stoke City in the Premier League, with Bertrand Traore scoring the opening goal for Chelsea and Mame Biram Diouf equalizing for Stoke City.

Three scientists, William C Campbell, Satoshi Omura, and Youyou Tu, have discovered and developed life-saving drugs, ivermectin and artemisinin, which have led to treatments for diseases affecting over 3.4 billion people worldwide, including malaria, river blindness, and elephantiasis.

The Nelson Mandela Foundation has called for President Jacob Zuma to be held accountable for his alleged role in "looting" state resources and undermining South Africa's democracy, as a court begins to hear a bid to prevent the release of a report by former anti-corruption chief Thuli Madonsela.
Miranda Hart made her West End debut in the musical "Annie" at London's Piccadilly Theatre, receiving positive reviews for her portrayal of the villainous orphanage owner Miss Hannigan.

Newcastle United secured a 2-0 win over Swansea, with Jonjo Shelvey helping to set up both goals and Aleksandar Mitrovic producing a hard-working performance, moving the Magpies out of the relegation zone at the expense of Swansea.

UK supermarkets, including Morrisons, Tesco, Asda, and Sainsbury's, have cut the price of diesel by up to 2p per litre, due to lower wholesale diesel costs and increased supply from refineries outside the UK, reversing a trend where diesel was typically more expensive than petrol.

The 70th UN General Assembly has highlighted the long-standing pressing issues facing Africa, including poverty, hunger, and conflict, while also showcasing the UN's crucial role in providing peacekeeping forces and addressing the continent's major worries, such as ending hunger and promoting sustainable development.

Suffolk police are searching for ecstasy pills containing the highly toxic class-A drug PMMA, also known as ParaMethoxyMethylAmphetamine, which has been linked to at least 22 deaths in the past year, and experts warn that even a different logo on the pills may not guarantee their safety.

UKIP donor and Leave.EU chairman Arron Banks has called for Nigel Farage to be "engaged once again" in the party, citing a need for radical change and a more professional approach to regain relevance.

The website Invisible Girlfriend and Boyfriend allows users to sign up and have a fake girlfriend or boyfriend created for them, with real people responding to their messages, and thousands of users have paid for the service for various reasons, including to get parents off their back, get a co-worker to stop hitting on them, make an ex jealous, or practice flirting.

Germany delivered a strong performance against Poland, immediately after a victory for Georgia, showcasing their attacking style and talent, but also had moments of vulnerability, providing an opportunity for Scotland to capitalize on their defensive lapses ahead of their match on Monday.

Bristol City and Blackburn Rovers played to a 1-1 draw, with Tammy Abraham scoring for City in the 22nd minute and Sam Gallagher equalizing for Rovers, leaving Rovers two points from safety with three matches remaining.

Scotland players, led by Strauss, want to give departing coach Vern Cotter a "good send off" by beating Ireland in their upcoming Six Nations match, with Cotter set to leave the Scotland job at the end of the season and be replaced by Gregor Townsend.
Celtic secured a 2-0 win over Kilmarnock, with Stefan Scepovic scoring twice after Kilmarnock's Alessandro Pascali was sent off in the 34th minute for a professional foul.

According to an international study by the OECD, Northern Irish pupils were more satisfied with their lives than their counterparts elsewhere in the UK, with an average satisfaction score of 7.24, while also exhibiting high anxiety levels, a lower rate of bullying, and a higher rate of excessive internet use, but also strong relationships with parents and teachers, and high academic ambitions.

Crystal Palace came from behind to defeat Everton 3-2, with goals from Fraizer Campbell, Yannick Bolasie, and Mile Jedinak, after Everton had taken an early lead through Romelu Lukaku, and Everton's Leighton Baines scoring a late penalty.

Gary Carter, a 36-year-old freelance sports journalist, was found with head injuries in Bethnal Green, London, after an altercation, and is heavily sedated while waiting for the swelling on his brain to go down.

Tinie Tempah, a British rapper with seven number one singles this decade, discusses his new album Youth, which he has been working on for over two years, and how reconnecting with his friends and roots helped him find his creative voice again after feeling disconnected from his early days in the grime scene.

Mobile operators, the UK government, and communications regulator Ofcom are set to discuss accelerating the allocation of spectrum to allow faster mobile download speeds, potentially enabling the launch of 4G networks in some places by May or June, rather than the previously expected end of the year.

The UK Conservative government has scrapped the policy of providing free school lunches to all children in the first three years of primary school, citing concerns over the cost, despite the policy being introduced by the previous coalition government in 2014.

Security camera footage in Tel Aviv showed a gunman, believed to be an Israeli Arab from northern Israel, taking an assault rifle out of his backpack and opening fire, resulting in at least four seriously injured people, before making off on foot, with Israeli security forces conducting a massive manhunt.

Dean Owens' great great grandfather Ambrose Salvona was found to be buried in Tomnahurich Cemetery in Inverness, Scotland, after Owens shared his family history with his audience, prompting local resident Judi Menabney to lead the search, which revealed that Salvona was associated with a dancing bear and had a colourful life in the Highland town.

Glastonbury festival has introduced sustainable, recycled stainless steel pint cups, made from 80% recycled steel and sourced from British manufacturers, as part of its efforts to promote sustainability and reduce plastic waste.

Rescue efforts in Nepal continue, with several survivors being pulled from the rubble, including a woman in her 20s, and the delivery of relief to remote villages is being hampered by bad weather, as the death toll has been reported to be 6,130.

Several major global banks, including JP Morgan, Standard Chartered, and Goldman Sachs, are planning to move hundreds to thousands of jobs from London to cities such as Dublin, Frankfurt, and Luxembourg in preparation for a potential no-deal Brexit.

After the shooting of 18-year-old Michael Brown by a white police officer in Ferguson, a mainly black suburb, on August 9, protests and riots erupted, with a five-hour curfew imposed, as the US justice department investigates the shooting and police moved in to break up the crowd after reports of people breaking into a barbecue restaurant.

Labour's Shadow Home Secretary Diane Abbott has criticized Prime Minister Theresa May's handling of police numbers, claiming that the cuts under her watch have let austerity damage her ability to keep us safe and put people at risk, a claim the Conservatives described as "desperate stuff" and said was "as desperate as she is hopeless under pressure" in response to her views on keeping us safe.

Wales suffered a 46-6 defeat to New Zealand in their final Test, their heaviest loss in nine years and 29th consecutive defeat to the All Blacks, but coach Warren Gatland believes the team will benefit from the experience and apply the lessons learned to future matches.

Six people, including a 17-year-old boy and his 50-year-old father, died after a whale-watching boat capsized, with the local community's quick response credited with saving 21 people from the 27 on board.

Myanmar's government and a group of rebel groups signed a collective agreement, which is not a nationwide ceasefire, with seven armed groups choosing not to participate, while only about half of the armed groups had made it to the start line.

A High Court judge in Northern Ireland ordered Facebook to remove a page targeting a sex offender, who had 15 convictions for sexual offenses, after ruling that the page's contents constituted prima facie harassment and risked infringing the man's human rights.

Apple has sent an email to publishers inviting them to join its forthcoming news app, requiring them to agree to terms that include indemnifying Apple in case of legal issues and allowing the company to place adverts next to their content without paying them, unless publishers explicitly opt out.

Residents of the US territory of Guam, which is home to about 6,000 troops and approximately 165,000 civilians, are expressing concern and anxiety over North Korea's threats to attack the island, with some residents planning to stock up on food and others feeling resigned to the possibility of a missile strike.

The European Space Agency's Sentinel-1b satellite, launched on a Soyuz rocket from French Guiana, will work alongside its predecessor to provide radar imagery of the Earth, monitoring applications such as pollution, icebergs, and land subsidence, while also contributing to the European Union's Copernicus programme.

The pound has risen 1% as markets are betting that Theresa May will win a larger majority in the upcoming election, which could give her more breathing room to potentially deliver a softer Brexit that would be less of a shock to the economic system, and the stock market is falling as a result of the pound's rise making foreign earnings worth less in sterling terms for the UK's largest companies.

A Czech woman, Pavlina Pizova, and her partner, Ondrej Petr, got lost on the Routeburn track in Fiordland National Park, New Zealand, after bad weather conditions, and Petr died in a steep ice slope accident, while Pizova spent almost a month in the Lake Mackenzie Hut before being found near Lake Mackenzie by a search team.

In Russia, millions of people, including Elena, a 40-year-old Muscovite, struggle financially, with 40 million Russians having loans or mortgages, and at least 10% of the total personal debt of 1 trillion roubles (£10.7bn; $16.7bn) being unrecoverable by banks.

James Holmes, a 24-year-old man, is accused of killing 12 and wounding 58 people in a shooting at a midnight showing of the Batman movie in Aurora, Colorado, prompting renewed calls for stricter gun regulations and a national conversation about gun control measures.

Art specialist Christopher Marinello, CEO of the Art Recovery Group, warns that it is feared hundreds of precious valuables have been smuggled out of Syria, and says that stopping the war and increasing awareness among collectors and dealers are part of the solution to address the crisis.

The Nuclear Accident Independent Investigation Commission's report concluded that the 2011 Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster was a "manmade" disaster, caused by a combination of collusion, lack of governance, and ingrained Japanese cultural conventions such as obedience to authority, groupism, and insularity, rather than a natural disaster.

The UK government's auto-enrolment programme has achieved a 95% compliance rate among small businesses, with 66% of employees now signed up, but concerns remain about the adequacy of employer contributions, which average just 3% of an employee's salary, and the need for further increases to ensure a decent retirement.

A new study published in Nature Geoscience estimates that the Earth's top 2km land surface holds approximately 180m deep of groundwater, with only 6% of this water being easily accessible and renewable, highlighting the need for better management of this vital resource.
Edinburgh has been chosen as the host city for the 2017 European Challenge Cup finals, which will take place over the same weekend as the European Rugby Champions Cup finals in Lyon, France.

Edward Snowden, the former CIA worker who leaked details of US surveillance programmes, remains in the transit zone at Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport, where he has been since arriving on June 23, after his lawyer stated that the temporary asylum application had been made but not processed, and no travel documents had been received.

Brazil's Attorney-General, Rodrigo Janot, has requested an investigation into former President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's alleged involvement in a multi-billion dollar kickback scheme at state-oil company Petrobras, where he is suspected of receiving illicit benefits and obstructing justice.

The UK government has rejected a recommendation to amend the Corporate Manslaughter Act to allow prosecution of the Ministry of Defence (MoD) for the deaths of three men who died after suffering the effects of hyperthermia during a 2013 SAS selection march, citing that existing arrangements worked effectively and the ability to bring civil claims for negligence, but also stating that it is difficult to apply the concept of manslaughter to the role of senior management in permitting and setting training parameters.

Leicester City, the defending Premier League champions, are in danger of becoming only the second defending English champions to be relegated, after being beaten by Millwall in the FA Cup, and face a Champions League last-16 first-leg trip to Sevilla on Wednesday.

HMRC is investigating dozens of footballers, agents, and clubs over potential irregularities in their tax affairs, particularly regarding image rights payments, with officials bringing in £158 million in yield over the last two years.

A scandal in Germany has erupted over the investigation of two journalists for treason after they published classified documents on online surveillance, highlighting concerns about the freedom of the press and the influence of government ministers over the courts.

UK Chancellor George Osborne's Budget speech omitted specific mention of the South East region, with only a few measures potentially benefiting the area, and was instead focused on announcements aimed at stimulating growth in the North and other regions, sparking accusations from politicians that he is taking the South East for granted.
Doncaster Rovers won 1-0 against Colchester United, with Tommy Rowe scoring in the first half to give Doncaster something to work with after the break.

Ross McEwan, the CEO of Royal Bank of Scotland, has stated that uncertainty caused by the EU vote is slowing down businesses, which will over time slow down banking, and that he does not expect interest rates to rise before 2017, while also noting that the British taxpayer may not recover the £45bn bailout provided to the bank in 2008 at the current rate.

Labour leader Ed Miliband has stated that he would not form a government with the SNP if it meant compromising on key issues, and SNP leader Nicola Sturgeon has responded by warning that Scottish voters would never forgive Labour if it allowed the Conservatives back into office.

Physics and planetary physics students Elliot Vale and Tia Mountain have designed an app called GeoRescue, which would provide information on natural disasters and guide people to safety using advanced maps services, GPS, and a distress signal feature that could potentially save lives.

The Scottish government's proposed Higher Education Governance Bill, which includes plans for the direct election of a chair for university courts, has been met with concerns from Sir Timothy O'Shea, who argues that the amendments are "inconsistent, incoherent and potentially very damaging", but he also welcomed other amendments to the bill.

Elena Hrabovenska, who came to England from Ukraine at the age of 19 in 2003, owns three shops in the UK, including one in Huntingdon and two in Peterborough, and is concerned about the potential disruption to her business due to a weaker pound and the threat of gridlock at Calais, which has already disrupted her fragile supply chain.

Dallas police received an anonymous threat against law enforcement and took precautionary measures to heighten security after the shooting of five police officers during a protest rally, with SWAT officers previously deployed at the main building.

Australian politicians, including Prime Minister Tony Abbott and Labor leader Bill Shorten, are calling for more to be done for refugees, with some, such as Josh Frydenberg, proposing a Kosovo-type solution for temporary housing, amidst a reaction to the image of a drowned Syrian boy, in the context of Australia's current refugee policies and commitments.

UKIP leader Nigel Farage unveiled a campaign poster attacking the Conservatives' pledge on immigration, stating that the target to cut net migration to the UK could not be achieved as long as Britain remained a member of the EU, as one cannot have an immigration policy or control who comes into Britain while being a member of the EU.

Gareth Southgate has been appointed as the permanent manager of the England national team, signing a contract reportedly worth up to £2m a year, after being interviewed and selected for the role following Sam Allardyce's departure after 67 days in charge, with Southgate having previously stepped up from his role as England Under-21s manager in September.

The FBI has ordered Apple to disable the security software on a dead gunman's iPhone, but Apple has refused, with tech leaders like Mark Zuckerberg and John McAfee, as well as companies like Facebook, Google, and Twitter, showing support for the company, citing concerns over encryption and the potential abuse of powerful tools.

Prince William praised his grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, as a "guiding example" of a good monarch in a BBC interview on the eve of her official birthday, while also discussing his own approach to royal duties and responding to recent criticism about his work ethic.

The new Star Trek film, Star Trek Beyond, briefly shows Hikaru Sulu being greeted by his male partner and daughter at the end of a voyage, a decision that has sparked a debate, with George Takei expressing disappointment that the character's sexuality was "outed" against his vision, while others, including the film's director Justin Lin and actor John Cho, argue it is consistent with Gene Roddenberry's vision.

Peterborough United won 4-1 against Bristol Rovers, with Jack Marriott scoring two goals in the 6th and 55th minutes, and another goal in the 80th minute, and Steven Taylor also scoring for Peterborough United, Rovers scoring a consolation goal 5 minutes from time, and Marriott scoring his treble in time added on.

Syria's antiquities chief has warned that the destruction of the Unesco World Heritage site of Palmyra by IS would be an "international catastrophe", as the group's militants were mounting an assault on the adjacent city of Tadmur, which was being defended by the Syrian army.

Passengers on a Thalys train, who were left in a compartment with limited access to the service area after staff locked themselves in a service area, claim that the train staff did nothing to help them during a shooting incident that unfolded after the train went through Brussels, and that the situation was eventually brought under control by Anthony Sadler's explanation, before being tackled by a group of heroic passengers, including Spencer Stone, Alek Skarlatos, Anthony Sadler, and Chris Norman.

GB Taekwondo's selection of Muhammad, ranked 59th in the world, over world number one Aaron Cook, has been ratified by the British Olympic Association (BOA), despite the BOA expressing disappointment over the handling of the issue and reserving the right to reconsider the nomination if new information emerges.

The investigation into the murders of British tourists Hannah Witheridge and David Miller on the Thai island of Koh Tao has reached a dead end, with police now admitting they have no DNA matches from the initial list of suspects, including 11 Burmese people.

Japan's rugby union is seeking to increase its popularity and national consciousness ahead of the 2019 Rugby World Cup, with the goal of raising interest and passion in the sport among the general public.

The trajectory of an uprising is significantly influenced by the distinction between independent and servile armies, with independent, professional armies often having appealing alternatives to bloodshed, while armies closely tied to autocratic regimes know that they have no institutional future if protesters get their way, and tend to use violence, making capacity-building in the absence of professionalization simply produce more efficient slaughter.

The UK's unemployment rate fell to 5.1% in the three months to November, its lowest rate since October 2005, with the employment rate reaching 74% and average weekly earnings growth slowing to 2% due to low inflationary pressure.

Middlesbrough secured their first home win of the season, with Gastón Ramírez and Stewart Downing scoring for Middlesbrough, as the team showed a good performance and commitment, and Bournemouth failed to maintain the intensity levels shown in their previous draw with Tottenham.

Felipe Massa of Williams experienced two left-rear wheel failures and Kevin Magnussen of Renault suffered a suspected broken left rear suspension during the first practice session of the Chinese Grand Prix.

Hibernian dominated Bonnyrigg Rose, scoring eight goals to one, with three goals in the first 13 minutes of the first half and five more in the second half, ultimately securing an 8-1 victory in their Scottish Cup match.

Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has stated that he believes homosexuals are "abnormal" or motivated by "mercenary reasons", and suggested that the issue can be addressed by improving the economy, while his government tries to persuade MPs to reject a proposed bill that would impose life imprisonment for homosexual acts and make it a crime not to report gay people.

Cardiff manager Neil Slade considers taking his team to a top-six finish this season would top any achievement in his career so far, but still views his previous play-off campaigns as highlights, and is aiming to reach the milestone of 1,000 managerial games, a feat he believes only a few of his colleagues in the club have achieved, with 23 or 24 managers having already reached this milestone.

Scotland's women's national team, led by 24-year-old forward Jennifer Evans, is in a strong position to qualify for the European Women's Championship, with victory against Iceland on Friday likely to all but secure their place in the tournament.

Claire, a former event-rider who was paralyzed from the chest down after a 2006 horse riding accident, is training to complete the London marathon using a robotic walking suit, with the aim of raising more than £50,000 for Spinal Research.

Jack Walsh, a 23-year-old film enthusiast from Northern Ireland, is working behind the camera for the popular YouTube channel Game Grumps in Los Angeles, where he shoots and directs commercials and is involved in the company's planned expansion into TV comedy.

The First Minister of Scotland, Nicola Sturgeon, has been ranked 50th on Forbes' list of the world's most powerful and influential women, with German Chancellor Angela Merkel topping the list for the sixth year in a row, followed by Hillary Clinton in second place and Janet Yellen in third.

An international team of scientists has found that almost 40 mammal species, including reindeer, can see ultra-violet light emitted by power lines, which they believe is a key factor in their avoidance of these structures, and could have a significant impact on wildlife globally.

Former employees and clients of the Kids Company charity have made allegations of sexual exploitation, including claims that some victims were ignored or intimidated by perpetrators when trying to report the abuse, and that staff were allegedly aware of complaints but their handling of the situation is disputed.

Paul Austin, a Leave voter, has expressed doubts about his original decision, influenced by recent events such as the Charlie Gard case and the Grenfell Tower fire, which have made him more uncertain about the UK's decision to leave the EU.

England's cricket team showed a vastly improved overseas display in the first Test against Pakistan in the UAE, compiling a total of 598-9 in their first innings, but ultimately fell short of a famous victory due to a combination of their own mistakes, including dropped wickets and a slow batting rate, and the match being ended prematurely due to fading light.

Celtic manager Brendan Rodgers praised the performances of new signings Oliver Ntcham and Kundai Benyu in a friendly match, highlighting their potential to become key players for the Scottish champions.

A shipment of 300 initial doses of an Ebola vaccine, developed by GlaxoSmithKline and the US National Institutes of Health, is expected to arrive in Monrovia on Friday, as part of the first potentially preventative medicine to reach one of the hardest hit countries, but experts warn that declining Ebola cases may make it difficult to determine the vaccine's effectiveness.
The match between Blackpool and Wycombe Wanderers ended in a 0-0 draw, with both teams creating several scoring opportunities but ultimately failing to find the back of the net.

The Australian government has agreed to a settlement of A$70m, covering costs estimated to be more than A$20m, shortly before the case was due to be heard in the Supreme Court of Victoria, regarding 1,905 asylum seekers who were held on Manus Island between 2012 and 2016.

Former Manchester United midfielder Paul Scholes, who had retired at the end of last season, has made a surprise return to the team, coming off the bench for the final 31 minutes of their 3-2 win over Manchester City, amidst an injury crisis that has beset the club.

Mike Young, a 70-year-old Welshman born in Barry, has spent his career creating popular characters, including SuperTed, and has now produced a feature-length animation, Norm Of The North, with his next project being a film about a former legend with his beloved Cardiff City football club.
